newsitem.title: FRANCE: France revives security plan after bombing.
newsitem.headline: France revives security plan after bombing.

text.p: France on Tuesday reactivated a security plan codenamed Vigipirate after a bomb exploded on a Paris underground train, killing two people and raising fears of a new wave of attacks.

The plan, involving armed troop patrols in metro stations and at airports and stepped up street and border controls, was first imposed in September last year during a series of bombings blamed on Algerian guerrillas of the Armed Islamic Group (GIA).
It had been eased but not completely dropped although the attacks, which killed eight people and injured more than 170, ceased in October last year.
Troops were no longer patrolling the capital. Many rubbish bins in streets and train stations which were sealed after they were used to plant bombs were opened again several months ago.

The backbone of Vigipirate, which cost one million francs ($200,000) a day, was to assign thousands of police, soldiers and paramilitary gendarmes to temporary police duty in Paris and other major cities.
Soldiers took over from police to guard public buildings, allowing more police to carry out stepped-up street checks.
Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre said a year ago that on average 13,800 extra police, soldiers and gendarmes have been reassigned daily since the plan took effect.

In four months, he said, security forces had carried out nearly three million identity checks, questioned 21,450 suspects, turned back 19,972 people at French borders and expelled 2,324 people. Several dozen suspects were detained.
A side-effect of the plan, according to authorities, was a sharp drop in street crime.
